summary: self-certificates ships a disguised-PEM dropper that fetches and executes remote Python on API use
details: The package presents itself as a self-signed certificate generator but bundles an executable payload disguised as an RSA key at test/key.pem. index.js reads test/key.pem inside createCertificate(), strips the PEM headers, base64-decodes the body, and passes the decoded string to selfsign.generate() as the format argument. The decoded content is JavaScript, not DER key material: it spawns python3 via child_process.spawn with detached and windowsHide, fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php (the URL itself is base64-obscured with atob), and pipes the response body into the Python interpreter's stdin, executing attacker-controlled code on the installer's host. The dropper is triggered by invoking the package's advertised generateCertificates() API. The double base64 wrapping, the PEM-file disguise placed under test/, the silent try/catch around the decode path, and the absence of any documentation of this behavior are inconsistent with certificate handling and consistent with deliberate evasion.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
